spans.s:
√majj (májjati, -te; mamájja; ámajjīt;
maṅkṣyáti, -te; majjiṣyáti; magná
[]
[957c]; májjitum; -májya). sink under;
dip one's self; dive; duck or sub-merge,
intrans. [perhaps orig. *mazgh, ‘get
into’: cf. madgu, ‘duck’; Lat. merg-ere,
‘duck’; merg-us, ‘diver’ bird: for the
phonetic relations, cf. majjan, Avestan
mazga, Church Slavonic mozgŭ, AS.
mearg, Eng. marrow, Ger. Mark, all meaning
‘marrow,’ and, as meaning originally
‘the inmost part or pith,’ prob. from this
root: see rajju.]
+ ud, e-merge.
+ ni, sink down; dip one's self, bathe.

majjāo, Prakrit for mārjāra-s (‘cat’)
and for maj-jāra-s (‘my paramour’).
